coreoffice.title: CoreOffice — ERP rewrite
coreoffice.description: The ERP I work on daily. I migrated a single CRA app to a Turborepo of Next.js apps so CoreOffice, the branch portal, and docs share one design system.
coreoffice.problem: ERP screens, shared UI, and docs lived in one CRA frontend. New modules were expensive, and the branch portal could not ship as its own app.
contribution: CRA → Next.js + Turborepo + TanStack Query, production stayed live
Split apps and packages so portal, ERP, and docs deploy independently
Branch portal: transparency, payslip, and collections uploads into CoreOffice
impact: Shared UI instead of duplicated frontend
Independent deploys for portal vs ERP

graph.title: Relationship graph — dense entities, explorable
graph.description: Designed and implemented the interaction model for exploring dense entity relationships with progressive node disclosure. Auditors could not read the same data as tables — used in ISMS certification workflows.
graph.problem: Entity relationships lived in dense tables. Auditors lost context trying to trace who connects to whom.
contribution: Designed pan, zoom, and progressive disclosure — nodes reveal neighbors on demand
Implemented the D3 force-directed graph as a CoreOffice menu module, not a standalone demo
Replaced table-tracing with visual paths for ISMS audit workflows
impact: Relationships that were unreadable in tables became traversable
Shipped inside the ERP, so auditors work where the data already lives

workflow.title: BPMN cartable — who holds the work
workflow.description: Per-user task inboxes driven by BPMN. Each organizational request shows who holds it now, where it goes next, and the full flow history — all inside CoreOffice.
workflow.problem: Requests had no visible owner. Staff could not see who holds a task, the next step, or the history without leaving the ERP.
contribution: Built per-user cartables routed by Camunda
Form.io renders the form from the process definition — no one-off form per request type
Current holder, next step, and full flow history in the same inbox
impact: Staff track a request from submission to completion without leaving CoreOffice
New process types reuse the same inbox and form shell

monitoring.title: BFF observability — the edge we actually run
monitoring.description: The loan platform and branch portal sit on a Next.js BFF we operate. Backend monitoring did not tell us if that layer was healthy. I added Prometheus, Grafana, and Graylog on our edge.
monitoring.problem: We owned the production edge, but we could only see the main backend. Failures on loan and portal were guessed from API errors.
contribution: Instrumented BFF apps with Prometheus exporters
Grafana dashboards for CPU, memory, and network on our edge
Graylog for structured log search and alerting
impact: The production edge we operate is inspectable — not only the main backend
Incidents on loan and portal are visible at the BFF

loan.title: Loan facilities — vama.melalbank.ir
loan.description: Customer-facing loan application site. Applicants submit requests in public; branch staff receive and process them inside CoreOffice cartables. A satellite of the same platform — not a separate product.
loan.problem: Loan requests needed a public SSR surface that still lands in branch cartables.
contribution: Public Next.js flows for requests and facility info
Submitted data flows into CoreOffice for branch review
impact: Applicants use a public site; branch staff process the same records internally

crypto.title: Crypto rate dashboard
crypto.description: Early structured frontend project while learning React Query and i18n — multi-language crypto dashboard with pagination, dark/light mode, and live market data. Kept here as a personal project, not enterprise work.
crypto.problem: I needed a real app to learn data fetching, i18n, and monorepo layout — not another tutorial clone.
contribution: First structured frontend project — React Query + i18n
Built in a Turborepo layout during the iApps internship
Real-time rates with paginated market views
impact: The project that made Turborepo and React Query concrete before CoreOffice
